# Flezha

> Distributed stateful relays — durable flow and steps compute

This map lists every guide page and the published API. Read it whole, then open
only the pages a task needs: each link is that page's full Markdown, next to this file.

## Start here

- [What is Flezha](what_is_flezha.md)
- [Running relays](running_and_testing.md)
- [CLI](cli.md)
- [Errors](errors.md)

## Getting started

- [What is Flezha](what_is_flezha.md): Flezha is a durable runtime for streams, workflows and agents.
- [Up and running](up_and_running.md): This page and the next two build the smallest complete Flezha deployment by hand: a controller, a runner of your own that serves an `echo` relay, and a file on each side of it.
- [Connect a plugin](connect_a_plugin.md): On this page you attach a file to each side of `my_echo`: lines added to one file go in, and their echoes land in another.
- [Stop and clean up](stop_and_clean_up.md): On this page you stop what the last two pages started, in reverse order: the plugins, the relay, the runner, then the controller.

## Core topics

- [Building blocks](building_blocks.md): Code that runs on Flezha is made of three pieces: tasklets, relays and runners.
- [Namespaces](namespaces.md): A namespace is a separate room inside one Flezha deployment.
- [Authorization](authorization.md): Authorization decides who may do what.
- [State](state.md): A tasklet can remember things between messages: a running total, a window of recent prices, the id of a reservation it may have to release.
- [Running relays](running_and_testing.md): A runner that registered a factory runs nothing yet.
- [Streams](streams.md): A stream is a relay that runs in flow, the default run: you start it once, and it handles each message the moment it arrives, for as long as it runs.
- [Workflows](workflows.md): A workflow is a piece of work made of steps that run in a fixed order: reserve the money, place the order, confirm the fill.
- [Sessions](sessions.md): A session is a relay instance that lives for as long as a conversation does: it has a beginning, it takes one message after another, and it remembers what was said.
- [Sending and calling](sending_and_calling.md): There are three ways to hand a relay an input.
- [Timers](timers.md): Some work is triggered by time rather than by input: a session that closes after 30 seconds of quiet, an idle buffer that flushes, a join that gives up waiting, a window that closes.
- [Durability and delivery](durability.md): Flezha writes down every change a tasklet makes to its state, and every step a workflow finishes, on the controller's disk as it happens.
- [Effectively once](effectively_once.md): A message that is lost is a question nobody answers.
- [Partitioning](partitioning.md): A relay started the usual way is one instance: all of its keys and all of their cells run on one runner, and that runner's machine is the limit.
- [MCP server](mcp_server.md): An AI coding assistant such as Claude Code, Cursor or Codex can build on Flezha with `flz mcp`, an MCP server that ships in every release.
- [Starter projects](starter_projects.md): A starter is a small, complete Flezha project in one SDK language, to grow into your own: one relay, a tasklet that keeps state, a test, and a README with the commands to build and run it.

## The CLI

- [CLI](cli.md): `flz` is the tool a controller is operated with: starting and stopping it, starting relays and sending them messages, managing namespaces, tokens and plugins, and reading state.
- [Controller commands](controller_commands.md): The groups that look after the controller itself: starting and stopping it, checking that it is up, the runners connected to it, its signals, and clearing its data.
- [Relay commands](relay_commands.md): The groups that work with relays: starting and stopping them, sending them input, reading their state, the inputs they gave up on, and the workflows started on a schedule.
- [Plugin commands](plugin_commands.md): `flz plugin` installs plugin packages, enables plugins and connects relays to them.
- [Access commands](access_commands.md): The groups that decide who may do what: namespaces and their quotas, the first admin, tokens, roles, and the audit trail that records each action.
- [Command reference](command_reference.md): Every `flz` verb with its usage line and what it does, by group.

## Configuration

- [Configuration overview](configuration.md): Flezha starts with no configuration.
- [Controller environment variables](environment_variables.md): Every variable the controller node reads, grouped by area.
- [Application env keys](application_env.md): Read via `Flezha.Config.get/1` by row name.
- [Relay settings](relay_settings.md): A relay is configured by one settings tree, declared in its class.
- [Plugin options](plugin_options.md): A plugin's options are its own settings: the URL it polls, the topic it publishes to, the file it writes.
- [Runner environment variables](runner_environment.md): Read by the runner process, not the controller node, so they are set where the runner runs.
- [Erlang VM arguments](vm_arguments.md): The VM the node runs in is configured before the application starts, so none of these can be a row of `lib/flezha/config/keys.ex` and `config/runtime.exs` never sees one.
- [Files and sockets](files_and_sockets.md)

## Plugins

- [Plugins](plugins.md): A plugin connects a relay to something outside Flezha: a file, a websocket, an HTTP endpoint, Kafka, a database.
- [Where a plugin runs](where_plugins_run.md): A relay plugin runs at the edge of the relays bound to it.
- [Enabling and binding](enabling_and_binding.md): `flz plugin` enables a plugin by name and binds relays to it.
- [Plugins from your own code](plugins_from_code.md): Enabling, binding, unbinding and disabling are on the SDK's `control()` handle, so an application can attach the plugins its own namespace needs.
- [Plugin examples](plugin_examples.md): Two setups from the guides: the echo's file plugins from [Connect a plugin](../../getting_started/connect_a_plugin.md), and the tradedesk's live feed into a partitioned relay.
- [Installing plugins](installing_plugins.md): A plugin that does not ship with the controller comes as a plugin package: a `.fpz` file carrying compiled code, the plugin's own application and every library it needs that the controller release does not ship.
- [Hooks](hooks.md): A hook is a moment at which the controller calls a plugin.
- [Writing a plugin](writing_a_plugin.md): A plugin of your own is an ordinary Elixir Mix project: it depends on `flezha` and on the libraries it needs, names its providers in its application environment, and is built into a plugin package (`.fpz`) that a controller loads when it starts.

## Plugin catalogue

- [File plugin](file.md): The file plugin makes a file a relay's input, to replay a log or load an export, or its output, to watch what a relay emits land somewhere `tail` can read.
- [HTTP poll plugin](http_poll.md): The HTTP poll plugin delivers a slowly-changing HTTP resource (runtime configuration, reference data, external state) onto a relay's entry channel.
- [HTTP push plugin](http_push.md): The HTTP push plugin sends a relay's outputs to an HTTP endpoint: a REST API, a webhook receiver, or any service that takes a request per record.
- [Websocket subscription source and output binding](websocket_subscription.md): The websocket plugin holds one websocket connection open for a relay: it injects every frame it receives into the relay's input, can change what the socket is subscribed to without tearing it down, and can send the relay's outputs back out on the same socket.
- [Relay-forward plugin](relay_forward.md): The relay-forward plugin sends one relay's outputs into another relay's input, in the same namespace.
- [Postgres output](postgres_output.md): The Postgres output plugin writes what a relay emits into a PostgreSQL database, in transactions.
- [Postgres poll source](postgres_poll.md): The Postgres poll source delivers the new, and optionally the changed, rows of one Postgres table onto a relay's entry channel, with no replication rights: it works on a managed database and on a read replica.
- [Webhook plugin](hook_webhook.md): The webhook plugin tells another service what happens in a namespace: a chat channel, an alerting tool, or any service that takes an HTTP POST.
- [HTTP server plugin](http_server.md): The HTTP server plugin puts a relay behind HTTP: a client sends a request, the relay's graph decides the answer, and the same connection can instead carry a stream of another relay's parts and outputs as server-sent events.
- [HTTP API plugin](http_api.md): The HTTP API plugin lets AI tools and scripts operate a controller from another process or machine.
- [Kafka consumer plugin](kafka_consumer.md): The Kafka consumer plugin delivers the records of Kafka topics onto a relay's entry channel.
- [Kafka producer plugin](kafka_producer.md): The Kafka producer plugin publishes what a relay ingests or emits to a Kafka topic.
- [RabbitMQ plugins](rabbitmq.md): The RabbitMQ plugins deliver the messages of a RabbitMQ queue onto a relay's entry channel, and publish a relay's outputs to a RabbitMQ exchange.
- [Postgres change capture](postgres_cdc.md): The Postgres change capture plugin delivers every inserted, updated and deleted row of Postgres tables onto a relay's entry channel, in commit order, after a first copy of the rows already there.

## Deploying

- [Deploying a controller](deploying_a_controller.md): The controller is the part of Flezha that decides and remembers.
- [Docker](docker.md): The image `flezha/flezha` holds the same release as the binaries, on Debian, and runs it as the user `flezha` (uid 1000).
- [Building from source](building_from_source.md): The [release archive](deploying_a_controller.md) is built for Linux x86_64.
- [Connecting a runner](connecting_a_runner.md): A runner is a program of your own that runs your relays.
- [Clustering](clustering.md): One controller can carry a whole application, but it is then a single machine to lose.
- [Kubernetes](kubernetes.md): A controller and its runners run on Kubernetes as they run in Docker or Docker Compose: the same images, the same settings as environment variables, and a shared folder for the Unix sockets the runner reaches the controller through.
- [Telemetry and metrics](telemetry_and_metrics.md): The controller describes what it does as signals: counts and measurements (metrics), and single happenings such as a refusal or a restart (events).

## Reference

- [Errors](errors.md): Every failure Flezha reports carries one shape, on every surface: the `flz` CLI, the published consumer API, the SDK administration door, spawn, a runner connect and every SDK.
- [A controller will not start, or will not stop](controller_will_not_start.md)
- [A runner cannot connect](runner_cannot_connect.md): `flz runner check` runs exactly the probe a runner runs.
- [Feature maturity](maturity.md): This record says which parts of Flezha are not yet settled.
